title: A chat you can steer
eyebrow: All six things in your last message are done, landed, and already running at your usual address.

questions.ask: Does the chat work the way you meant?

options.label: Yes — close both jobs
options.say: The chat reads right now. Close them.

options.label: Not yet
options.say: Something in the chat is still wrong — I'll say what.

questions.note: Your usual address is rebuilt and restarted, so it is already showing all of this.

questions.ask: Your own commands, skills and rules now apply inside these chats, exactly as in a terminal. Keep it?

options.label: Keep it
options.say: Keep my own commands, skills and rules inside the app's chats.

options.label: Turn it back off
options.say: Go back to a plain session in the app: no commands, no skills, none of my rules.

questions.note: There is no half of this the tool offers: the commands and the skills arrive with the settings that also carry your rules and your gates. Off means the slash menu is the tool's own 40 entries and none of yours.

content.label: Your six complaints
content.lead: Each one, and what it does now.

rows: I see nothing while it is working
19 seconds of work with nothing on the screen, ten of them frozen mid-tool
a line at the foot the whole time: what it is doing, and how long
The address does not say where I am
the open chat lived in the screen's memory only
the chat and the open card are in the address; a pasted address opens the same thing
Back does not work
switching tabs left no history entry at all
every move by hand is a step Back undoes
Clicking a chat resumes it and it jumps to the top
a click started an agent and re-sorted the list
a click draws the conversation and starts nothing; the first message wakes it
A ticket should open beside me, not on the board
a chip threw you onto the board tab
the card slides over whatever you are reading, and Back closes it
No mode, no model, no skills, no commands
the session deliberately loaded none of your machine
all four in the writing box, acting on the chat you are in
A dropped picture cannot be looked at
a 48-pixel thumbnail and nothing else
click it for full size, Escape to close, and a cross to take it back out

content.label: What it looks like
content.lead: Taken from the running screen, on your own board.

shots.caption: Working: a moving mark, what it is doing, and the seconds — where your eye already is
A slash lists your own commands and skills, with their descriptions
The model and the permission mode sit in the writing box and change the chat you are in
A ticket opens over the chat, which is still there behind it

content.label: Read by someone who did not write it
content.lead: Two readings, twelve objections, all twelve answered in code.

rows: Closing a ticket left a Back press that did nothing
one dead press per ticket looked at
An edit in the ticket panel did not move the card behind it
a stale board for fifteen seconds after every edit
Clicking a terminal chat twice made a second copy of it
five duplicates already on your board
Opening a chat that never touched a ticket read it off the disk again every time
the ticket tool re-run on every click
A sleeping chat offered a mode and model that changed nothing
a silent click
Withheld reasoning drew an empty heading
a label with nothing under it, in the picture that was meant to be the proof

blocks.text: The other six were the seconds counter carrying one tool's clock onto the next, a mid-chat skill discovery taking the model menu away, Escape closing the panel two ways at once on the board, dead code left behind, unread state in the driver, and the proof picture committed under a name the job did not promise.

content.label: Two traps worth knowing
content.lead: Both measured, both in the tool rather than in us.

blocks.text: Turning every skill on explicitly leaves the agent the skill tool and nothing else: a turn then ends silently with no answer at all. Your skills load anyway, with your settings, so that switch is left alone.

A session says nothing about itself — not even that it is ready — until the first message is sent to it. The menus are asked for the moment the chat exists instead, and until this was found, a chat announced Ready over an agent that was still working.

decisions.title: The address carries where you are, as parameters
decisions.why: Prettier paths need the server to answer for addresses that only exist at runtime; this app ships as files inside the binary. Parameters carry every effect you asked for — a link that opens the same thing, a Back that goes back — and needed no server change.

decisions.title: A click is a read, and only a message wakes an agent
decisions.why: Your own words. It also means a chat you click keeps its place in the list, because being looked at is not activity.

decisions.title: One ticket panel for the whole screen
decisions.why: So a ticket reads the same wherever you open it from, and the board and the panel share one reading of the board rather than each keeping its own.

decisions.title: The chats load your own machine
decisions.why: There is no way to have your commands and skills without the settings that carry them. That is the second question above.

decisions.title: What it is doing goes at the foot, not in the badge at the top
decisions.why: The badge was already there and you still saw nothing: it is at the far end of the pane from where you read and type.

next.if_nothing: Both jobs sit waiting on your look; nothing else moves on them.
